attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is #ffffff on background var(--surface). In the default light theme --surface is #ffffff, so the "Embargo until ..." label renders white-on-white and is invisible. The feature's core purpose fails in the default theme.

The unpublish control is a <span> with an onClick handler and no role, tabIndex, keyboard handler, or accessible name. Keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot reach or activate it, which violates the stated WCAG 2.1 AA requirement (2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value).

The icon-only control has aria-hidden on its icon and no aria-label or visually hidden text, and the CSS defines no focus-visible style. Even if made focusable, it would announce nothing meaningful and show no focus indicator.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: aria-label / sr-only text on the unpublish control; ABSENT: :focus-visible rule in DraftRow.module.css

attacks.claim: The one-click unpublish action is shown to every user viewing the queue for any published draft, but the artifact shows no client or server permission check. Without a server-side authorization check, users who lack unpublish rights can remove live stories.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any authorization/role check on onUnpublish or on rendering the unpublish control; the condition is only `draft.status === "published"`

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch and no error state. If the API call fails, the story stays live, the row does not change, and the promise rejects unhandled. The editor may believe the story was pulled when it was not.
attacks.evidence: `if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);` with no error handling

attacks.claim: Unpublish removes a live story with no undo and no visible audit trail in the artifact. The confirm dialog mitigates the accidental-click risk, so this is non-blocking.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: audit logging or undo path for unpublish

attacks.claim: The embargo state is computed once per render from new Date(). A badge can remain shown after its lift time until the row re-renders for another reason.
attacks.evidence: `const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();`

attacks.claim: The PR makes no claim of contrast checking, screen-reader testing, or keyboard testing, even though WCAG 2.1 AA is a release requirement. The white-on-white defect above would have been caught by a simple contrast check.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: contrast measurements, a11y test results, or keyboard test plan in PR description
